hotspots.title: Manuel Adorni’s corruption scandal deepens
hotspots.blurb: Argentina's Chief of Staff Manuel Adorni faces escalating allegations of illicit enrichment after admitting to undeclared assets, including $500,000 in Bitcoin. Opposition parties are demanding his resignation, and the scandal has sparked a political crisis for President Javier Milei’s government.
hotspots.affect: This scandal commands disproportionate attention due to its moral charge, polarized contention, and the high stakes for Milei’s reform agenda, which is already under scrutiny.

hotspots.title: AfD’s internal extremism controversies
hotspots.blurb: Germany’s far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) faces internal and external backlash over extremist rhetoric, including calls to abolish compulsory schooling, alleged ties to neo-Nazi groups, and controversial statements by party leaders. The party’s rise in polls has intensified scrutiny ahead of state elections.
hotspots.affect: The AfD’s extremist framing and moral panic over its policies have made it a dominant theme in German political discourse, with cross-party condemnation amplifying its charged narrative.

hotspots.title: PP-Vox coalition deals reshape Spanish regional governments
hotspots.blurb: Spain’s conservative Partido Popular (PP) and far-right Vox are forming coalition governments in multiple regions, including Castilla y León and Andalusia. The deals prioritize anti-immigration policies, deregulation, and cultural conservatism, sparking backlash from opposition parties and civil society groups.
hotspots.affect: The coalition deals carry high affective investment due to their moral charge, polarized contention, and the sense that Spain’s political landscape is shifting toward far-right influence.

hotspots.blurb: Hungary’s ruling Fidesz party, led by Viktor Orbán, is grappling with internal turmoil following its electoral defeat. Opposition party Tisza, led by Péter Magyar, is pushing for reforms, including overhauling state media and replacing intelligence chiefs, while Orbán faces criticism for his authoritarian leadership style.
hotspots.affect: The power struggle in Hungary commands attention due to its moral charge, polarized contention, and the sense that the country’s political future is at stake.
